about: The short state of the work between the orchestrator and the GPU worker. Read it first after any restart; docs/PIPELINE.md says how the two work. Only the orchestrator edits it. A goal is open until the worker has confirmed the outcome on real hardware, then closed; it is with_owner when three rounds did not settle it or the decision is the owner's to make.

goals.name: The memory step
goals.decides: Which line Setup shows for a graphics card smaller than the model, and for which cards
goals.outcome: Three things, each confirmed on the published site against the real app. (1) --diffusion-fa is what the picture engine needs on any card; Setup shows the step for every kind of computer and puts it away once it is saved (WO-01, WO-02). (2) The line saves --diffusion-fa --offload-to-cpu; the two option sets fail alike on one piece, so nothing argues for dropping the second (WO-02). (3) For the standard model on a 12 to 16 GB card the line also saves --max-vram 8, which makes the engine split a one-piece outfit: 13 made in 13 where the two options alone had failed 5 in 8 (WO-03, WO-04). Not measured, and so not acted on: any other card, any other value, the larger model with a limit, and how much ordinary memory --offload-to-cpu needs on a 16 GB computer.

goals.name: Knowing the step is done
goals.decides: Which field of the app's model list shows the saved options, so Setup can put the step away
goals.outcome: WO-02 confirmed it on the published site against the real app: the step is hidden for a model with --diffusion-fa saved, shown for one without under every kind of computer, and gone once its line has been run and Connect pressed. The app's real model-list entry is pinned in test/local.test.js.

goals.name: The download readout
goals.decides: Whether Setup's size, speed and time left match the app's own window
goals.outcome: WO-01: the readout matched the app's own window at three points on a 19.3 GB download (the window counts in 1024s and labels them GB and MB/s; the page counts in decimal GB and megabits a second). Nothing in the page changed for it.

goals.name: What a local model keeps
goals.decides: How many pieces it keeps faithfully, and what Setup and the README should promise
goals.outcome: WO-01: with four pieces or fewer no piece was missing in 18 different pictures, so the cap stays at four. Exactness suffers instead (lettering redrawn by the smaller model, odd shapes made ordinary, a hat's colour shifted, jewellery added); the README now says so.

goals.name: The larger model
goals.decides: Whether Flux-2-Klein-9B-GGUF is worth suggesting, and for which cards
goals.outcome: WO-01 measured it on a 12 GB card: Flux-2-Klein-9B-GGUF ran with --diffusion-fa, took about one and a half times as long, and kept a lettered print right where the smaller model garbled it. The owner's answer (2026-11-26) was that quality is the priority, so Setup suggests the larger model from 12 GB up, uses a model that is already downloaded before asking for a 19 GB download, and tells someone on the standard model that the larger one keeps prints better. Not measured: a 16 GB computer, where the larger model's files may not fit in ordinary memory with --offload-to-cpu.

goals.name: A new picture each time
goals.decides: Whether making the same outfit again on a local model gives a different picture
goals.outcome: WO-02 confirmed it on the published site: three requests for one outfit gave three files, three seeds in the engine's log and three pictures that differ to the eye.

goals.name: Bottoms added to a lone top
goals.decides: Whether naming the added pieces outright stops a local model inventing malformed bottoms
goals.outcome: WO-03 confirmed it on the published site and in the checkout: with the instruction naming the added pieces, 28 one-piece pictures in 28 (24 from the standard model, 4 from the larger) showed whole, plain, full-length trousers and plain shoes, against 4 malformed in 11 before.

goals.name: Odd shapes on a local model
goals.decides: Whether naming a piece, or a note, makes a local model keep an unusual shape, or whether that is the model's limit and the page should say so
goals.outcome: WO-05 measured it on the published site: a name and a note both change what the local models draw, and the note most. On the larger model the unnamed clown shoes were swapped for plain shoes in 3 pictures of 3; named 'oversized clown shoes' they were drawn as clown shoes, bigger than ordinary but short of the piece, in 3 of 3; with a note about their size as well they were oversized as in the piece in 3 of 3. The standard model went the same way, weaker (with the note, 1 of 2 oversized). So it is not the models' limit, and the page now says so where it matters: with a local model the tip under the pieces asks for a name and what is unusual, and warns that an unnamed piece is often swapped for a plain one, and a tip under Notes asks for anything unusual to be described there. Not separated: whether the word 'oversized' in the name or the instruction changes since WO-04 did the first part. The note brought small side effects (a band at the hems once, jewellery once).

goals.name: The new flat lay wording on a local model
goals.decides: Whether a local model can give a clean flat lay: with the sentence about adding missing basics left out, with a note about gaps, or not at all
goals.outcome: Three orders on the published site (WO-05, WO-06, WO-07; 39 flat lays and comparison pictures on the 12 GB card). What was fixed: the trousers and other shoes nobody supplied came from the sentence that lets the model add missing basics (5 flat lays of 6 with it, 0 of 12 without); the page now reads the pieces' names and offers basics only for what they leave open, and WO-07 confirmed the one new sentence on the card: with only shoes missing, shoes added and no trousers in 4 of 4, where the old sentence drew trousers under supplied jeans in 1 of 2. What was not: the pieces lie on each other (5 of 6, and 4 of 4 with a note about gaps); the standard model draws more shoes than the supplied pair in 4 of 5 and the larger in 1 of 7; added shoes came as two pairs in 1 of 4. These are taken as the models' limit for flat lays. The page says, with a flat lay on a local model, that 'On a model' keeps the pieces best, and no other wording will be tried. Not run: only shoes named (the sentence for missing bottoms), and names the page does not recognise.

goals.name: The Claude check with a real key
goals.decides: Whether the optional check works from the page, catches real faults and passes good pictures, and what it costs; and so whether its instructions or the page's sentence about its cost change
goals.so_far: WO-08 (28 checks with the owner's key, $0.91; 16 Google pictures): run from Node as the page builds it, the check answered 28 times in 28 on the default model. It passed 4 good pictures twice each, the oversized clown shoes among them, and failed 8 of 10 kinds of planted fault twice each, naming the fault every time (wrong lettering, a redrawn print, recoloured laces, recoloured jeans, a replaced piece, jeans cut to shorts, a doubled piece, odd shoes made ordinary). It passed two faults twice each with every field empty: jeans folded in half in a flat lay, and a head cut off at the mouth. A check cost about 3 cents and took 2 to 6 seconds. Changed on that: the check's instructions now fail a piece that cannot be seen whole and a figure not in frame head to shoes; the page's cost sentence says a few cents instead of 'roughly doubles'; the runner's check is off unless a variable is named. WO-09 runs the same fourteen pictures again. Still unproven: the browser's own path to Anthropic. The cloud workspace's test browser cannot reach it (a certificate error from the workspace's network); a preflight from here shows Anthropic allows the site's origin and the headers the check sends; a real browser on an ordinary network has not tried it.

in_flight.with: the cloud session that ran WO-08

next: The download readout between two files: the app reports no progress for about half a minute and the page then shows the size alone, which reads as stuck. It can only be confirmed during a real download, so it waits for the next one.
Setup, 'What kind of computer is this?': choosing 'Choose…' by hand shows the advice for the page's own guess (WO-02, surprise 6). Small; fix with the next change to Setup.
--max-vram for cards that were not measured: an 11 GB card is likely the most fragile of all, and nothing is known for 8, 16 or 24 GB. Needs other hardware, which the worker does not have.

The standard local model added a wristwatch in 2 of its 4 'on a model' pictures in WO-05, against the instruction's 'no hats, bags, watches, jewellery'. Small beside a lost piece; look at it if a later order makes pictures on a model anyway.

The standard local model drew the supplied shoes as three shoes in 3 flat lays of 4 (WO-06), past 'Show every supplied item exactly once'. Flat lays there are already advised against; not worth an order on its own.
dead_ends: --offload-to-cpu on its own as the memory step: on a 12 GB card it failed every outfit of two to four pieces, exactly as no options did (WO-01).
"Try again with fewer pieces" as advice for a failed local picture: with the card nearly full, one piece was the outfit that failed and adding a second made it work (WO-01).
Choosing between --diffusion-fa alone and both options to make a one-piece outfit safer: with part of the card held they fail alike, for the same stated reason (WO-02).
--max-vram -1 (reserve a gigabyte of whatever is free): the engine works the figure out once at load and still plans one block; 2 of 5 with a gigabyte held (WO-03).
--max-vram 6: it works, but every picture's last stage fails once and is redone in tiles (WO-03). 8 leaves that stage alone.
open_questions: For the owner, when convenient: on the published site in your own browser, paste the Claude key under 'Optional: double-check every picture' in Setup and make one outfit. Does Setup say the key works, and does a verdict ('Matches your pieces' or 'Off in places') appear under the picture? That is the one part of the check no session here can reach.
owner_priorities: 2026-11-26: quality is the priority. Where faithfulness to the pieces trades against speed, download size or a few cents, choose faithfulness (CLAUDE.md, Rules).
for_the_owner: WO-02, surprise 7: the worker started LM Studio's background service by mistake (it ran LM Studio's command-line tool to list models) and its attempt to close it was refused. It is still running on the owner's computer; quitting LM Studio closes it.
